aboutWhatItDoes: HealthYarn lets you ask everyday health questions in Yorùbá, Nigerian Pidgin, or English and hear general health information in a natural Nigerian voice — matching pre-approved clinical guides first and using strictly guardrailed general guidance when a valid health question falls outside the core guide.
aboutWhatItDoesNot: HealthYarn does not diagnose illness, prescribe medicines, or calculate personal dosages. In any emergency or danger sign, go straight to a clinic.
aboutPrivacySummary: No accounts for public users. No third-party trackers. Voice clips are processed in memory and discarded immediately.
sttFailedMessage: Could not hear clearly or reach voice service. Please browse a topic below or try again.
aboutPillar1Body: Yorùbá, Nigerian Pidgin, and English spoken naturally—the way people actually talk at home.
aboutPillar2Body: No reading required and no typing needed. Speak your question out loud and listen calmly.
aboutPillar3Body: Every answer is written from WHO and Nigeria FMOH guidance and checked by clinical and language reviewers.

problemHeading: Health advice shouldn't need good English.
problemBody: Doctors are few and always busy. Leaflets and medicine labels are in English. So many people wait too long, take medicine the wrong way, or follow what the neighbour said. HealthYarn gives everyone someone to ask.
stat3Label: is a common wait to see a doctor
howHeading: As easy as sending a voice note.
step1Body: Tap Yoruba, Pidgin or English. The app talks you through it.
step2Body: Hold the microphone and say your question, like "My child has been stooling since yesterday. What should I do?" Or just tap a picture.
step3Body: A natural Nigerian voice answers in your language. Replay it or slow it down whenever you like.
safetyBody: HealthYarn never diagnoses, prescribes medicines, or gives personal drug dosages. Core answers are written from World Health Organization and Federal Ministry of Health guidance and checked by clinicians and native speakers. For valid health questions outside the core library, AI general guidance is clearly labelled and always directs you to a clinic when needed. Non-health or unclear questions are not guessed.
safetyBodyUnreviewed: In this preview build, the voice guidance flow is active while clinical and language review sign-off is flagged as under review.
safetyWill1: explain common health problems in simple words
safetyWill2: tell you when to go to a clinic urgently
safetyWill3: explain how to take medicines safely
safetyWillNot3: replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist
dangerCalloutBody: If what you describe sounds serious, HealthYarn stops and tells you to go to a health facility now, and shows clinics near you.
topicsBandHeading: What you can ask about today.
languagesBody: The voices are made with Spitch and YarnGPT for Nigerian languages. Tap to hear the same answer in each language.
privacyHeading: What you say stays with you.

privacyPoint2Body: Your voice is used to understand your question, then deleted.
privacyPoint3Body: We only count which topics people ask about, so we can improve.
partnersHeading: Working in a clinic, pharmacy or community programme?

faq1A: No. It gives general health information that health professionals have checked. It does not examine you or diagnose you. If you feel very unwell, go to a clinic.
faq2A: It is free to use. It uses a small amount of data, and answers you have already heard work without internet.
faq3Q: Do I need to read or type?
faq3A: No. You can do everything by talking, listening and tapping pictures.
faq4A: No. Your recording is used to understand your question and is then deleted.
faq5A: Yoruba, Nigerian Pidgin and English. More are planned.
faq6Q: What if it does not understand me?
faq6A: It will tell you, and show a few questions to choose from. It will not guess.

aboutSec1Lead: Good health information should not depend on how well you read English.
aboutSec2Body: In many Nigerian homes, the person caring for a sick child or an ageing parent speaks Pidgin or Yoruba every day, but the clinic leaflet, the medicine label and the health advert are in formal English. Doctors are few and busy, so there is rarely time to ask questions. We built HealthYarn so that anyone can ask a health question the way they would ask a trusted neighbour, out loud and in their own words, and hear an answer they can understand and trust.
aboutSec2Quote: If you can send a voice note, you can use HealthYarn.
aboutSec3Title: Every answer passes through people before it reaches you.
aboutSec3Step1: Written in simple English from World Health Organization and Federal Ministry of Health guidance
aboutSec3Step2: Checked by a doctor, nurse or pharmacist
aboutSec3Step2Demo: In demo review before clinical sign-off
aboutSec3Step3: Translated into Pidgin and Yoruba and checked by native speakers
aboutSec3Step3Demo: Prepared in Pidgin and Yoruba while native-speaker review is ongoing
aboutSec3Step4: Voiced and listened to again before it goes live.
aboutSec3Note: Verified answers come directly from the clinician-reviewed guide library and are clearly badged. When a valid health question falls outside the core guide, HealthYarn provides clearly labelled guardrailed general health information without diagnosing or prescribing.
aboutSec3NoteDemo: This preview pairs clinician-drafted core guides with clearly badged guardrailed AI general health info for wider questions. It never diagnoses, prescribes, or replaces a clinic.
aboutSec4Title: What HealthYarn will and won't do
aboutSec4Will1: explain common health problems in simple words
aboutSec4Will2: tell you when to go to a clinic now
aboutSec4Will3: explain how to take medicines safely
aboutSec4Will4: work with little data, and offline for answers you've heard.
aboutSec4Wont2: prescribe medicine or tell you a dose
aboutSec4Wont3: replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist
aboutSec4Wont4: keep your voice or ask for your name.
aboutSec4Emergency: In an emergency, don't wait for an app. Go to the nearest health facility.

aboutSec7Point3: We only count which topics are asked about.
aboutSec8Body: We started with five topics and three languages. Next we want to add Igbo and Hausa, more topics such as immunisation and nutrition, a WhatsApp version, and a phone line for people without smartphones. We also want to test HealthYarn with a primary health care centre.
